events.title: Rise of Sumerian Civilization
events.description: Southern Mesopotamia (present-day Iraq) saw one of the world's earliest urban civilizations—the Sumerian civilization. City-states like Ur, Uruk, and Lagash developed cuneiform writing, the wheel, the plow, and irrigation systems. Sumerians built ziggurats and invented the sexagesimal system and calendar, laying foundations for human civilization.

events.title: Akkadian Empire Established
events.description: Sargon the Great conquered Sumerian city-states, establishing Akkadian Empire, world's first multi-ethnic empire. Akkadian language became diplomatic language, influencing entire ancient Near East. Sargon established centralized government, promoting trade and cultural exchange.

events.title: Ur Third Dynasty
events.description: Ur-Nammu established Ur Third Dynasty, unifying Mesopotamia. This period saw peak in law, literature and architecture. Code of Ur-Nammu was one of oldest surviving written law codes. Ur's ziggurat was masterpiece of Mesopotamian architecture.

events.title: Hammurabi Rules Babylon
events.description: King Hammurabi unified Mesopotamia, establishing Babylon's First Dynasty. He promulgated the famous Code of Hammurabi with 282 laws carved on stone stele. The principle of 'an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth' influenced later legal systems. Babylon became the ancient world's cultural and commercial center.

events.title: Hittites Sack Babylon
events.description: Hittite King Mursili I sacked Babylon, ending Old Babylonian Dynasty. Kassites subsequently ruled Babylon for over 400 years. Though Mesopotamia was politically divided, culture continued.

events.title: Rise of Assyrian Empire
events.description: Neo-Assyrian Empire rose with capital at Nineveh. Assyrians built powerful army using iron weapons and chariots. King Ashurbanipal established one of world's earliest libraries. Assyrian Empire conquered vast territories from Egypt to Persian Gulf.

events.title: Neo-Babylonian Empire Established
events.description: Nabopolassar established Neo-Babylonian (Chaldean) Empire. His son Nebuchadnezzar II conquered Judah, destroyed Jerusalem's First Temple, deporting Jews to Babylon (Babylonian Captivity).

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar II's Reign
events.description: Nebuchadnezzar II was Neo-Babylon's greatest king. He rebuilt Babylon, constructed Hanging Gardens (one of Seven Wonders of Ancient World) and Ishtar Gate. Babylon became ancient world's most magnificent city with population of 200,000.

events.title: Persian Conquest of Babylon
events.description: Persian King Cyrus the Great conquered Babylon, ending the Neo-Babylonian Empire. Cyrus freed captive Jews, allowing them to return to Jerusalem. Babylon became an important city in the Persian Achaemenid Empire.

events.title: Alexander Conquers Mesopotamia
events.description: Alexander the Great defeated Persian King Darius III at Battle of Gaugamela, conquering Mesopotamia. Babylon welcomed Alexander, hoping he would restore city's glory. Alexander planned to make Babylon capital of his empire, but died there in 323 BCE.

events.title: Seleucid Dynasty Rule
events.description: After Alexander's empire divided, Seleucus I established Seleucid Empire controlling Mesopotamia. Greek culture blended with local traditions. Seleucia on Tigris built as new capital, competing with declining Babylon.

events.title: Parthian Conquest of Mesopotamia
events.description: Parthian Empire conquered Mesopotamia from Seleucids. Parthia became Rome's greatest eastern rival, controlling Silk Road trade. Ctesiphon on Tigris became Parthian capital and major commercial center.

events.title: Sasanian Persian Rule
events.description: Ardashir I overthrew Parthians, establishing Sasanian Empire. Sasanians made Ctesiphon their capital, built magnificent Taq Kasra arch. Zoroastrianism became state religion. Sasanian Persia rivaled Byzantium for centuries.

events.title: Arab Conquest of Mesopotamia
events.description: Arab Muslims defeated Sasanian Persia at the Battle of Qadisiyyah, conquering Iraq. Iraq gradually Islamized and Arabized. Kufa and Basra became new Muslim cities and military bases.

events.title: Ali Moves Capital to Kufa
events.description: Fourth Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib moved capital from Medina to Kufa, Iraq. Kufa became Shi'a Islam's political center. This marked beginning of Sunni-Shi'a split intensification.

events.title: Battle of Karbala
events.description: Imam Hussein (Prophet Muhammad's grandson) was martyred at Battle of Karbala by Umayyad forces. This tragedy became central to Shi'a Islam identity. Karbala became holiest pilgrimage site for Shi'a Muslims.

events.title: Founding of Baghdad
events.description: Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur established the new capital Baghdad on the Tigris River, meaning 'God's Gift.' Baghdad adopted circular design, becoming the center of the Islamic Golden Age. By the 9th century, Baghdad's population reached one million, the world's largest and most prosperous city.

events.title: Harun al-Rashid's Reign
events.description: During Caliph Harun al-Rashid's reign, the Abbasid Dynasty reached its zenith. Baghdad became a center of scholarship, culture, and trade. The opulent court life described in 'One Thousand and One Nights' reflects this period. Harun patronized scholars translating Greek, Persian, and Indian texts.

events.title: Al-Ma'mun and House of Wisdom
events.description: Caliph al-Ma'mun established House of Wisdom (Bayt al-Hikma) in Baghdad, translating Greek, Persian, Indian texts into Arabic. Scholars like al-Khwarizmi (father of algebra) gathered here. This was intellectual peak of Islamic Golden Age.

events.title: Islamic Golden Age
events.description: Baghdad became world's intellectual center. Scientists and philosophers like al-Razi, al-Farabi advanced medicine, philosophy, mathematics, astronomy. Baghdad's universities and libraries attracted scholars worldwide. Translations preserved Greek classical knowledge.

events.title: Seljuk Turks Occupy Baghdad
events.description: Seljuk Turks occupied Baghdad, Caliph became figurehead, real power held by Seljuk sultans. Though politically declining, Baghdad remained cultural and religious center.

events.title: Mongols Destroy Baghdad
events.description: Mongol commander Hulagu besieged Baghdad, massacring hundreds of thousands. The last Abbasid Caliph al-Musta'sim was executed, ending 500 years of Abbasid Caliphate. The House of Wisdom was burned, countless manuscripts destroyed. The Tigris River turned black with book ink. This was the greatest disaster in Islamic civilization history.

events.title: Ilkhanate Rule
events.description: Mongol Ilkhanate ruled Iraq as part of Mongol Empire. Later Ilkhans converted to Islam, attempting to restore economy and culture. But Iraq never fully recovered former glory.

events.title: Timur Sacks Baghdad
events.description: Timur (Tamerlane) sacked Baghdad, massacring tens of thousands. This dealt another devastating blow to already declining Iraq. Baghdad's population plummeted, never regaining Islamic Golden Age prosperity.

events.title: Ottoman Conquest of Baghdad
events.description: Ottoman Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent conquered Baghdad from Safavid Persia. Iraq became Ottoman Empire's eastern frontier province. Baghdad's strategic importance made it repeatedly contested by Ottoman and Persian forces.

events.title: Persian-Ottoman Contest
events.description: Safavid Persia temporarily captured Baghdad, but Ottomans reconquered it in 1638. This warfare devastated Iraq's economy and population. Treaty of Zuhab (1639) established Ottoman-Persian border along Zagros Mountains.

events.title: Ottoman Direct Rule
events.description: After crushing Mamluk dynasty in Baghdad, Ottomans imposed direct rule, reforming administration. Iraq divided into Baghdad, Basra, Mosul vilayets. Tanzimat reforms attempted to modernize but met local resistance.

events.title: WWI Outbreak and British Invasion
events.description: World War I erupted, Britain invaded Iraq to protect Persian oil and Suez Canal. British Indian forces landed at Basra, beginning Mesopotamian Campaign. This marked end of Ottoman rule in Iraq.

events.title: British Occupy Baghdad
events.description: British forces under General Maude entered Baghdad, ending 400 years of Ottoman rule. Britain promised to 'liberate' Arabs but actually planned colonial rule. Iraqis gradually became disillusioned with British rule.

events.title: Iraqi Revolt
events.description: Iraqis launched massive revolt against British occupation, Sunni and Shi'a united against colonial rule. British brutally suppressed revolt using aircraft and poison gas, killing over 10,000. Revolt forced Britain to reconsider Iraq policy.

events.title: Establishment of Iraqi Kingdom
events.description: Britain installed Faisal I (son of Sharif Hussein of Mecca) as King of Iraq. Iraq became constitutional monarchy under British mandate. Though nominally independent, Britain controlled foreign affairs and military.

events.title: Anglo-Iraqi Treaty
events.description: Britain and Iraq signed treaty, Britain retained military bases and oil interests, but promised to support Iraq's League of Nations membership. Treaty was unpopular with Iraqi nationalists who saw it as continued imperialism.

events.title: Independence and League of Nations Membership
events.description: Iraq gained formal independence, became first Arab state to join League of Nations. But Britain retained significant influence through military bases and advisors. King Faisal I attempted to forge unified Iraqi national identity.

events.title: Simele Massacre
events.description: Iraqi army massacred thousands of Assyrian Christians in Simele Massacre. This genocide targeted Assyrians who supported British. Event revealed ethnic and religious tensions within new state.

events.title: Rashid Ali Coup and British Invasion
events.description: Pro-Axis nationalist Rashid Ali al-Gaylani staged coup, expelled British. Britain invaded Iraq, crushed rebellion, reinstalled pro-British regent. This demonstrated Iraq's continued lack of sovereignty.

events.title: Joins Arab League
events.description: Iraq was founding member of Arab League. League aimed to coordinate Arab policies and oppose imperialism and Zionism. Iraq played active role in Arab nationalist movement.

events.title: First Arab-Israeli War
events.description: Iraq sent troops to fight newly declared Israel in first Arab-Israeli war. Iraqi forces fought in West Bank but Arab defeat shocked Arab world. Palestinian refugee problem deeply affected Arab politics including Iraq.

events.title: Baghdad Uprising
events.description: Mass demonstrations erupted in Baghdad protesting poverty and British influence. Police opened fire, killing hundreds. Though suppressed, uprising revealed monarchy's fragility and growing discontent.

events.title: Baghdad Pact
events.description: Iraq joined Baghdad Pact (later CENTO), anti-Soviet alliance with Turkey, Iran, Pakistan, UK. This pro-Western alignment was unpopular with Arab nationalists, contributing to 1958 revolution.

events.title: July Revolution Overthrows Monarchy
events.description: The Free Officers Organization under Brigadier Qasim staged a coup, overthrowing the Hashemite monarchy. King Faisal II and pro-British Prime Minister Nuri al-Said were executed. The Republic of Iraq was established, withdrew from the Baghdad Pact, and aligned with the Soviet Union.

events.title: Qasim's Rule
events.description: Qasim implemented land reform and social reforms, withdrew from pro-Western alliances. He allowed Communist Party activity but refused merger with Nasser's Egypt. Qasim's dictatorship and economic difficulties bred discontent. He was killed in 1963 Ba'ath coup.

events.title: Kurdish Rebellion Begins
events.description: Kurdish leader Mustafa Barzani launched armed rebellion demanding Kurdish autonomy. This began decades-long Kurdish conflict. Northern Iraq became battlefield, hundreds of thousands of Kurds displaced.

events.title: Ba'ath Party First Coup
events.description: Ba'ath Party and military officers overthrew Qasim in bloody coup. Qasim was executed. Ba'athists brutally suppressed communists. But internal divisions led to Ba'ath losing power after only nine months.

events.title: Ba'ath Party Seizes Power
events.description: Ba'ath Party staged second coup, permanently seizing power. Ahmad Hassan al-Bakr became president, Saddam Hussein his deputy and real power behind throne. Ba'ath established one-party authoritarian state.

events.title: Nationalization of Oil
events.description: Iraq nationalized Iraq Petroleum Company controlled by Western companies. Oil revenues flooded in, funding massive infrastructure projects and military buildup. Oil wealth gave Ba'ath regime economic independence and regional influence.

events.title: Algiers Agreement
events.description: Iraq and Iran signed Algiers Agreement, Iraq made border concessions in exchange for Iran stopping support to Kurdish rebels. Kurdish resistance collapsed, hundreds of thousands of Kurds fled to Iran. This temporary reconciliation set stage for Iran-Iraq War.

events.title: Saddam Hussein Becomes President
events.description: Saddam Hussein forced President Bakr to resign, formally taking power. He launched a great purge, executing hundreds of Baath Party officials and officers, consolidating personal dictatorship. Saddam established a personality cult, comparing himself to Nebuchadnezzar and Saladin.

events.title: Iran-Iraq War Begins
events.description: Saddam tore up the Algiers Agreement, invading Iran, trying to seize Khuzestan oil region and overthrow Khomeini's regime. The war bogged down into stalemate, evolving into attrition warfare. Both sides used chemical weapons and human wave tactics. The war lasted 8 years, causing a million casualties.

events.title: Halabja Chemical Attack
events.description: Iraqi forces used chemical weapons against Kurdish town of Halabja, killing 5,000 civilians. This was worst atrocity of Anfal Campaign, genocidal campaign against Iraqi Kurds. Saddam's crimes against humanity shocked world.

events.title: Iran-Iraq War Ends
events.description: Iran-Iraq War ended with UN-mediated ceasefire after eight years. Over million casualties, neither side gained territory. War left Iraq with massive debt and militarized society. Saddam sought new conquest to restore prestige.

events.title: Invasion of Kuwait
events.description: Saddam ordered Iraqi forces to invade Kuwait, occupying the entire country within 6 hours. Saddam declared Kuwait Iraq's 19th province. Invasion motives included debt, oil prices, and territorial ambitions. This action shocked the world, triggering international condemnation and sanctions.

events.title: Gulf War
events.description: A 34-nation US-led coalition launched Operation Desert Storm, liberating Kuwait. After 42 days of air campaign, the ground war lasted only 100 hours. Iraqi forces were crushed, burning Kuwaiti oil wells during retreat. The war demonstrated US military technological superiority, changing Middle East power balance.

events.title: Shi'a and Kurdish Uprisings
events.description: After Gulf War, Shi'a in south and Kurds in north rebelled against Saddam. US encouraged uprisings but didn't intervene. Saddam brutally crushed revolts using chemical weapons and helicopter gunships, killing tens of thousands. This betrayal scarred Iraqi memory.

events.title: UN Sanctions
events.description: UN imposed comprehensive sanctions on Iraq, devastating economy and society. Infant mortality soared, infrastructure collapsed. Oil-for-Food Program allowed limited humanitarian relief. Sanctions killed hundreds of thousands but failed to topple Saddam.

events.title: No-Fly Zones
events.description: US and allies established no-fly zones over northern and southern Iraq to protect Kurds and Shi'a. Iraqi Kurdistan gained de facto autonomy. Frequent clashes between Iraqi forces and coalition aircraft continued throughout 1990s.

events.title: Operation Desert Fox
events.description: US and UK launched four-day bombing campaign against Iraq for non-cooperation with UN weapons inspectors. Iraq expelled inspectors. This presaged 2003 invasion.

events.title: Kurdish Civil War
events.description: Two major Kurdish parties KDP and PUK fought civil war over control of northern autonomous region. Saddam exploited divisions to invade, severely damaging Kurdish resistance. After US mediation conflict subsided, Kurdish region split into two governments.

events.title: 9/11 Aftermath
events.description: Though Iraq had no connection to 9/11 attacks, Bush administration listed Iraq as part of 'axis of evil,' accusing Saddam of possessing WMD and supporting terrorism. US began planning war against Iraq.

events.title: US Invasion of Iraq
events.description: The US and allies like Britain launched the Iraq War, codenamed Operation Iraqi Freedom. US forces began with 'shock and awe' airstrikes, ground forces attacked from Kuwait. The Bush administration claimed to overthrow Saddam, eliminate WMD threats (later proven nonexistent), and bring democracy to Iraq.

events.title: Fall of Baghdad
events.description: US forces entered Baghdad, Saddam's regime collapsed. Saddam's statue in Firdos Square was toppled, becoming an iconic moment. But Iraq subsequently descended into chaos, government institutions paralyzed, massive looting and violence erupted.

events.title: Bush Declares 'Mission Accomplished'
events.description: President Bush declared end of major combat operations on aircraft carrier, with 'Mission Accomplished' banner. But this declaration was premature, Iraq actually descended into prolonged insurgency and sectarian violence. Most US casualties occurred after this.

events.title: US Dissolves Iraqi Army
events.description: US administrator Paul Bremer dissolved Iraqi army and Ba'ath Party, leaving hundreds of thousands unemployed and resentful. This catastrophic decision fueled insurgency, many ex-soldiers and officers joined resistance. Iraq lost security forces and institutional knowledge.

events.title: Iraqi Insurgency
events.description: Sunni insurgency, Shi'a militias, Al-Qaeda in Iraq waged guerrilla war against US forces and Iraqi government. Suicide bombings, IEDs became daily reality. Over 4,000 US soldiers and hundreds of thousands of Iraqis killed. Iraq descended into sectarian civil war.

events.title: Saddam Captured
events.description: US forces captured Saddam in a 'spider hole' near Tikrit. He was disheveled, no longer having dictator's dignity. Saddam's capture was a symbolic victory but failed to quell the insurgency. He was later tried in Iraqi court.

events.title: Saddam Executed
events.description: Saddam Hussein was sentenced to death by Iraqi court for crimes against humanity, hanged on Eid al-Adha. The execution was filmed by mobile phone and leaked, showing Shia guards taunting him. The execution intensified sectarian hatred, Saddam became a symbol of Sunni resistance.

events.title: Sectarian Civil War
events.description: Iraq descended into full-scale sectarian civil war. Al-Qaeda in Iraq bombed Shi'a holy sites, Shi'a militias conducted ethnic cleansing. Baghdad neighborhoods were divided by sect. Tens of thousands killed monthly. Iraq teetered on brink of complete collapse.

events.title: US Troop Surge
events.description: US sent 20,000 additional troops to Iraq, implementing counterinsurgency strategy. Surge combined with Sunni Awakening reduced violence. But gains were temporary, failing to address Iraq's fundamental political divisions.

events.title: Sunni Awakening Movement
events.description: Sunni tribes in Anbar and elsewhere turned against Al-Qaeda, allying with US forces. This dramatically reduced violence. But Iraqi government failed to integrate Awakening fighters, sowing seeds for ISIS rise.

events.title: US Withdrawal
events.description: Last US combat troops left Iraq, ending nearly nine-year occupation. Iraq was left with weak institutions, sectarian divisions, and unresolved conflicts. Prime Minister Maliki's increasingly authoritarian and sectarian rule alienated Sunnis.

events.title: Sunni Protests
events.description: Sunnis in Anbar and other provinces protested Maliki government's discrimination and marginalization. Government violently cracked down. Sunni grievances created fertile ground for ISIS.

events.title: ISIS Captures Mosul
events.description: Islamic State (ISIS) captured Iraq's second-largest city Mosul, tens of thousands of Iraqi troops fled without fighting. ISIS leader Baghdadi declared a caliphate at Mosul's Great Mosque. ISIS occupied one-third of Iraqi territory, shocking the world.

events.title: War Against ISIS
events.description: Iraqi government forces, Kurdish fighters, Shia militias, and US-led international coalition fought ISIS. Combat was extremely brutal, cities turned to ruins. After three years of war, ISIS was expelled from Iraqi territory, but at enormous humanitarian cost.

events.title: Yazidi Genocide
events.description: ISIS massacred thousands of Yazidis in Sinjar, enslaving thousands of women and girls. This genocide prompted US airstrikes. Kurdish peshmerga and PKK fighters rescued many trapped Yazidis. UN classified ISIS actions as genocide.

events.title: Battle for Mosul
events.description: Iraqi forces launched nine-month campaign to retake Mosul from ISIS. Battle was Iraq War's deadliest combat, Mosul reduced to rubble. Thousands of civilians killed. Liberation of Mosul in July 2017 marked turning point against ISIS.

events.title: Victory Over ISIS Declared
events.description: Iraqi Prime Minister Abadi declared complete defeat of ISIS, recovering all territory. But ISIS turned to underground insurgency, continuing attacks. Iraq faced enormous challenges of reconstruction and reconciliation.

events.title: Kurdistan Independence Referendum
events.description: Iraqi Kurdistan held independence referendum, 93% voted for independence. Baghdad and neighbors rejected it. Iraqi forces retook disputed territories including Kirkuk. Kurdish dream of independence was crushed.

events.title: First Post-ISIS Elections
events.description: Iraq held first elections after ISIS defeat. Muqtada al-Sadr's coalition won most seats. Low turnout reflected Iraqi disillusionment. Forming government took months, demonstrating Iraq's political dysfunction.

events.title: October Protest Movement
events.description: Young people launched massive protests in Baghdad and southern cities, demanding improved services, fighting corruption, and ending foreign interference. Security forces brutally cracked down, over 600 died. Protests forced Prime Minister Abdul-Mahdi to resign.

events.title: US Assassinates Soleimani
events.description: US drone strike at Baghdad airport killed Iranian General Qassem Soleimani and Iraqi militia leader Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis. This dramatically escalated US-Iran tensions. Iraqi parliament voted to expel US troops, but vote was non-binding.

events.title: Kadhimi Becomes Prime Minister
events.description: Former intelligence chief Mustafa al-Kadhimi became PM after months of political deadlock. He promised reforms and to curb militia power. But faced enormous challenges of economic crisis, COVID pandemic, and Iranian influence.

events.title: Parliamentary Elections
events.description: Iraq held early elections demanded by protesters. Sadr's movement won most seats. Record low turnout showed Iraqi despair. Iran-backed militias disputed results, tensions escalated.

events.title: Political Deadlock
events.description: Iraq suffered year-long political deadlock, unable to form government. Sadr and Iran-backed Coordination Framework struggled for power. Sadr's supporters stormed parliament. Iraq lacked functioning government for over year.

events.title: Sudani Becomes Prime Minister
events.description: After Sadr withdrew from politics, Mohammed Shia al-Sudani of Coordination Framework became PM. Government formation took over year. Sudani pursued pragmatic policies, balancing Iranian and Western interests.

events.title: US Withdrawal Negotiations
events.description: Iraqi government negotiates with US on American troop withdrawal. About 2,500 US troops remain in Iraq, nominally fighting ISIS. Pro-Iran militias demand complete US withdrawal. But security concerns and ISIS threats persist, withdrawal prospects unclear.
